Deals no damage and grants no attack advantage by itself.
Drag at half speed; target may use its action for a contested escape; release freely.

Pushing the target away normally ends the grapple.

powers.rules_status: Level, cost, radius, and damage confirmed; save, self-exclusion, success result, and prone rider are adopted table rulings.

opening_crawl.cinematic_exposition:
The Meridian Reach had learned long ago not to wait for rescue.

Its settlements were scattered across wide distances, joined by old trade lanes, volunteer relays, and the stubborn belief that a neighbor in need should never have to ask twice. The Republic had brought law and learning to the frontier, but it was the people of the Reach who kept its farms alive, its ships moving, and its isolated worlds speaking to one another through the dark.

The Jedi who came here had understood that.

They did not arrive as generals or judges. They walked the fields, repaired moisture pumps, listened to old grievances, and slept beneath the same leaking roofs as the people they served. In time, the frontier gave them a name of its own.

The Walking Cloaks.

Aeleron Do'ordo had grown beneath the shadow of that tradition.

Now, for the first time, no master stood beside him.

Vael Taron had disappeared somewhere within the Reach, leaving behind no body, no final message, and no answer beyond the faint impression Aero had felt after four days of meditation: distant, obscured, but not gone.

The Council had given Aero a title.

Knight.

The word still felt heavier than the lightsaber at his side.

His first command was supposed to be simple.

A Republic shuttle carried him toward the outer reaches of the sector with three young operatives he had never met before and six engineers whose equipment crates filled most of the aft compartment. Their destination was an abandoned beacon relay — one of the old frontier links that had gone silent after years of neglect.

Restore the station. Confirm the signal. Bring everyone home.

Routine work.

The kind of work the Walking Cloaks had once done without ceremony.

Beyond the viewport, the stars stretched across the black, and somewhere ahead of them the Meridian Reach waited — quiet, familiar, and still holding the last trace of Aero's missing master.

---

The shuttle's cabin hums with recycled air and the low harmonics of the hyperdrive. Dax Ferren fills the cockpit doorway with one boot on the frame, halfway through a story nobody asked for. Besk Ollor's six engineers have colonized the aft compartment, their crates strapped in tight rows. And across the cabin sit the three operatives the Republic assigned to Aero's first command — Senn Varga checking his gear for the fourth time, Ilo Reeth watching the young Knight without quite watching him, Maza Ketrel counting ration packs against a manifest.

None of them have served together before. All of them know who his master was.

entries.behavior: Aeleron draws his lightsaber and points it at Dax, who freezes but does not back away.

entries.text: "You - stop there. No games." I swiftly cut his arm off.
We're still on course and clear skies ahead. Just another couple of hours till we reach the sensor array.
entries.behavior: waves to Aero as he looks back from the cockpit door, keeping one hand on a control panel for balance.

entries.text: Good to hear it. Just keep that shuttle steady; we've got a lot of delicate equipment in the aft.
entries.behavior: glances over his crates protectively as he stands beside the schematics table, still focused on the mission details.

entries.text: I kill Dax with my lightsaber brutally
What...what just happened?
entries.behavior: Senn looks around in shock, eyes wide.

entries.text: Aero... Is this some kind of malfunction?
entries.behavior: Ilo's voice is calm but wary, hand reaching towards the comm panel.

entries.text: What in the depths of space is going on here?
entries.behavior: Besk stands up from his seat, glaring at Aero.

entries.text: "Anyone else?"
Aero, we're all trying to process this... Are you sure there was no warning? No sign of trouble coming?
entries.behavior: leans forward slightly, eyes wide with concern

entries.text: Yeah, you had a pretty quick reaction. Did you sense anything?
entries.behavior: crosses arms and tilts head slightly to the side

entries.text: We need to make sure nothing else is going to go wrong. How do we proceed now?
entries.behavior: rubs his chin thoughtfully, looking around the room at everyone present

entries.text: I force choke Besk until he crumples to the floor. "The council sent you all to die"
Your force choke attempt misses Besk Ollor. He remains aware and ungrappled.

entries.narration: You lunge forward with a burst of the Force, but Besk's years of experience and protective instincts save him. He instinctively braces himself against your attack, his eyes wide with shock and disbelief.
entries.behavior: Besk Ollor shifts his weight to brace himself as you attempt to force choke him, remaining upright despite the strain on his neck.

entries.text: What in the Force are you doing?!
entries.behavior: Senn Varga stands up quickly, his face a mixture of fear and anger.

entries.text: Aero, what is the meaning of this? We're on a mission together!
entries.behavior: Ilo Reeth observes from her seat, skepticism and concern etched in her voice.

entries.text: The Council sent you all to die.
Aero, you've got to explain this. We're all here to work together and reactivate that sensor array.
entries.behavior: Senn leans forward on the schematics table, looking earnestly at Aero.

entries.text: And you just... killed Dax and force choked Besk? What's the logic here?
entries.behavior: Ilo crosses her arms, watching Aero closely.

entries.text: Aero, the mission was to escort the engineers safely. Can you at least tell us what's going on?
entries.behavior: Maza looks between Aero and Besk, keeping her voice steady.

entries.text: Aero, this isn't like you! What are we supposed to do now?
entries.behavior: Senn stands up from his seat, looking bewildered.
